learning_objective: 🎯 Discover where businesses get the money to start, run, and expand! Understand the difference between 'Owner's Funds' and 'Borrowed Funds'.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Owner's funds (like Equity shares, Retained earnings) belong to the owners, carry high risk, and stay with the business forever. Borrowed funds (like Loans, Debentures) are loans that must be repaid with fixed interest, regardless of profit or loss.

Equity shareholders are the real owners; they take the highest risk and have voting rights. Preference shareholders get a fixed rate of dividend before equity shareholders and have a priority claim if the company closes down.
It's the portion of net profits that is not distributed to shareholders as dividends but is kept in the business for future use (expansion). It's also called 'ploughing back of profits'.
A document issued by a company acknowledging a debt. Debenture holders are creditors of the company. They get fixed interest (even if the company makes a loss) and have no voting rights.

fun_activity.title: 🍕 The Pizza Funding
fun_activity.instructions: You want to buy a ₹500 pizza. You use ₹200 from your piggy bank (Retained Earnings). You sell a 50% share of the pizza to a friend for ₹200 (Equity Shares). You borrow ₹100 from your brother and promise to pay him ₹110 tomorrow (Debenture/Loan). That's business finance!

exam_tips: 📌 Differentiate clearly between Shares (Ownership, Dividend, Voting rights) and Debentures (Creditors, Interest, No voting rights).
📌 Retained earnings are considered the cheapest source of finance because there are no explicit costs (like interest or dividend payouts) involved.
📌 Trade Credit is a short-term financing source where a supplier allows a buyer to purchase goods now and pay later.
quick_recap: ⭐ Commercial Paper is an unsecured promissory note issued by highly rated companies to raise short-term funds.
⭐ Factoring is a financial service where a business sells its accounts receivable (invoices) to a third party (factor) at a discount.
⭐ Global Depository Receipts (GDRs) and American Depository Receipts (ADRs) are used to raise equity capital from international markets.
